content:
sara: Started a quick onboarding pass for mako-embed-lite int6-perchannel (onnx). Ran standard openset + tail holdouts. Head looks fine but tail recall@1 down ~3.9% vs fp16 baseline. Clusters look smeared in UMAP.

ethan: can you paste the high-level numbers and which eval sets?

sara: Quick paste from the summary.csv for the overnight run:
```
set,recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,median_cosine,silhouette
head,0.893,0.957,0.972,0.81,0.34
tail,0.745,0.861,0.908,0.69,0.14
overseas,0.712,0.847,0.893,0.67,0.13
overall,0.835,0.912,0.939,0.75,0.23
```
Note: "overseas" is a small multilingual holdout we keep for regressions.

priya: tail median_cosine drop (0.81 -> 0.69) is telling. Did you keep whitening and L2-normalization the same as fp16?

sara: I used whiten=True, l2_norm=True, same pipeline. Microbatching kept at 128. Quant config: per_channel int6 symmetric, outlier_clamp=4.0.

ethan: two quick checks: 1) rerun with asymmetric per-channel, 2) run with whiten=False to see if whitening amplifies quant noise.

sara: queued both. Commands: ```
python eval/run_embeddings.py --model mako-lite-int6.onnx --holdout holdouts/tail.jsonl --batch 128 --whiten True --norm True --quant perchannel_sym --clamp 4.0
python eval/run_embeddings.py --model mako-lite-int6.onnx --holdout holdouts/tail.jsonl --batch 128 --whiten False --norm True --quant perchannel_asym --clamp 4.0
```

dasbot: scheduled jobs 1781112301 and 1781112302 (trail slots). ETA ~12m.

(bench-bot): results incoming...
```
job_id,exp,recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,silhouette
1781112301,asym_perch,0.761,0.869,0.912,0.16
1781112302,whiten_off,0.772,0.873,0.915,0.18
```

sara: whiten_off surprisingly better than asym. That suggests whitening fit may be sensitive to quant-induced noise. I also dumped neighbor-cosine diffs: mean delta -0.07, but heavy tail.

priya: can you run a small calibration step: compute per-channel scale excluding top 0.5% outliers and try clamp=3.0? Also try norm_clip=0.95 to limit norm variance.

sara: will run 3 quick probes: clamp3, clamp4+norm_clip, clamp3+whiten_smallcomp (whiten fit on 50k instead of 500k).

(bench-bot): probe summary:```
job,config,recall@1,recall@5,silhouette
1781112321,clamp3,0.773,0.875,0.18
1781112322,clamp4_normclip,0.781,0.878,0.20
1781112323,clamp3_whiten50k,0.792,0.884,0.22
```

ethan: clamp3_whiten50k is the best. small whitening comp set seems to avoid over-correction. Good signal.

priya: next steps: 1) bootstrap CI for recall@1 vs fp16 on tail (1000 resamples), 2) extract top-1 flips for manual annotation (100 examples), 3) run knn-stability varying k=1..10 and seed sweep.

sara: started bootstrap job 1781112340 and flip-extract 1781112341. flip file uploaded: gs://redwood-evals/mako/ints/flips-1781112222.jsonl

dasbot: bootstrap done 1781112340: recall@1 delta (int6 clamp3_whiten50k - fp16) = -0.8% (95% CI [-1.4%, -0.2%]) — still a small but significant regression.

priya: small regression but narrowing. Human labels will tell if flips are benign. If many flips are paraphrases/duplicates then it's okay to ship.

ethan: also run downstream reranker MRR on a sampled set. Quant noise can affect initial retrieval which then affects reranker compute budget.

sara: launching reranker MRR check. Also planning a 1% canary with a traffic-split for dedicated infra if we decide to proceed. Will add a model-config flag to allow whiten_comp_size per deployment.

priya: thanks. One more: check multilingual holdout results (overseas). If multilingual suffers, we might need to keep fp16 for those customers or apply different quant profiles.

sara: overseas quick numbers for clamp3_whiten50k: recall@1=0.728 (fp16 0.741) — small drop but within noise.

ethan: ok. please upload the annotated flips and bootstrap outputs to the ticket and mark as "blocking" only if >50% true regressions in human labels.

sara: will update ticket INF-3412 with links and add PR for whiten_comp_size flag. Closing loop once labels and reranker numbers are in.

priya: nice investigation, short plan looks actionable.

sara: thanks all.
